title: Arignar Anna and the Overnight Drama 'Or Iravu': The Dialogue Revolution (1946)
summary: In 1946, C. N. Annadurai penned his revolutionary socio-political play Or Iravu (One Night) in a single overnight sprint, forever transforming Tamil theater into a vehicle of social justice.
keywords: Historical Dialogue 196: காந்தியும் கப்பல் பயண உரையாடல்களும்
full_text:
In 1946, the Tamil stage was dominated by mythological fantasies filled with kings, miracles, and celestial courtiers that completely ignored the crushing realities of rural poverty.

A theatrical troupe approached C. N. Annadurai with an urgent plea: they needed a compelling social drama to stage within a week to revitalize their bankrupt company.

Anna accepted the challenge without hesitation. Sitting down at dusk with stacks of blank paper and a pot of coffee, he wrote continuously through the night without sleeping. By dawn, he handed over a complete three-hundred-page manuscript: the revolutionary drama Or Iravu ('One Night').

When staged, Anna's scorching dialogues electrified audiences, stripping bare feudal hypocrisy:
"The pet dog of the wealthy landlord feasts upon bread soaked in golden ghee, while the hungry infant of the impoverished laborer whose sweat produced that very harvest dies of starvation on the temple steps! Is this divine destiny, or the ruthless crime of an unjust society?"

The play became an unprecedented cultural sensation, later adapted into a landmark film by AVM Studios. Through Or Iravu, Anna transformed modern theatrical arts into an engine of socio-economic awakening.
